notes: T538 (429 logged as model failure): a worker killed by an account-level 429/401/403 is recorded in docs/infra/model-perf.md as that model failing its task. Landmark L1 (measurement integrity) — blocks Stage 2's grand race, whose lanes are scored from this file. THE DEFECT: tools/dispatch_verify.py classified an outcome by what verification found (nonce absent, deliverables missing, row untouched), not by whether the model was ever reached. A connect-time 429 produced the same evidence as a model that ignored its brief, so the ledger attributed an infrastructure fact (a billing limit) to glm-5.2 — ~80 records, all `verified=fail fail=row`. THE FIX (committed f56d751, tools/dispatch_verify.py): (1) PROVIDER_REFUSAL_SIGNATURES + provider_refusal_reason(root, task_id) read the worker log untracked/log/t<id>.log (written by bin/dispatch's nohup redirect, so it carries the refusal block for any provider) and classify 429/401/403/quota/auth/connection-failure into provider-429 / provider-auth / provider-connection. Conservative by construction: the status-code signatures anchor to line start (`^\s*429\b`), which distinguishes the real `429: {"message":...}` block from a PID (`[runner] pid 42994` — ruled out by the \b boundary) or a mention inside a prompt; 401/403 require an auth keyword nearby. (2) verify_dispatch: when the worker died (rc != 0) AND the log shows a refusal, the perf tuple becomes (..., 'unreached', reason) instead of (..., 'fail', fail_check) — applied only to the worker-died-with-row-open paths (bare rc!=0 and T-ID open-row rc!=0); a clean-exit no-op stays fail, and a worker that closed the row before a non-zero exit was clearly reached and stays fail, so the distinction cannot launder genuine failures. (3) record_perf now emits `verified=unreached reason=<reason>` (vs `verified=fail fail=<reason>` vs bare `verified=pass` — the pass/fail line formats are byte-identical to before). (4) heal_dispatch appends `"unreached": <reason>` to the heal assertion record when the worker died of a refusal, so T536's keeper backoff can tell a lane-down heal from an ordinary dispatcher heal (the forward-looking counterpart of the retroactive {"correction": true} precedent in dispatch-heals.jsonl).
